records.role_detail: book says the action on Sirt1 is indirect
records.quote: Its main targets seem to be activation of sirtuins, deacetylases that activate transcription of antioxidant enzymes and promote mitogenesis
records.notes: Book describes it as 'a polyphenol found in grapes and red wine'. Same page adds 'recent data indicate that its action on Sirt1 is indirect'; page 282 says it 'may not activate sirtuins directly'; page 283 calls it 'an stimulator of Sirt1'. Enzyme class taken from the book's word 'deacetylases'.

records.quote: resveratrol may not activate sirtuins directly but thorugh activation of AMPK
records.notes: Statement is hedged in the book ('biochemical studies indicate that ... may not'). The typo 'thorugh' is in the original.

records.quote: upon low energy levels, increased NAD+ concentration activates Sirt1, which in turn operates on FOXO3
records.notes: drug_kind 'endogenous ligand' is my classification; the book does not label NAD+. Page 281 calls sirtuins 'NAD+-dependent protein deacetylases'. Physiological signalling statement, not a drug.

records.quote: is reflected in the rise of the AMP/ATP ratio that triggers AMP-dependent activation of AMPK
records.notes: drug_kind 'endogenous ligand' is my classification; the book states it as a rise of the AMP/ATP ratio, not as AMP binding. Physiological signalling statement, not a drug. Page 280 (Fig. 1 caption) calls AMPK 'the ATP sensor'.

records.mechanism_book_wording: effects ... are due to its plasma membrane receptors (MT1 and MT2)
records.quote: The effects of melatonin on sleep rhythm are due to its plasma membrane receptors (MT1 and MT2) in the suprachiasmatic nucleus.
records.numbers_detail: Slow-release formulation (Circadin) 'increases its plasma concentration over the following 8-10 h' (PDF page 274)
records.notes: The word 'agonist' is not used for melatonin itself; the role is inferred from the next sentence, which calls ramelteon and agomelatine 'specific agonists' of these receptors. Book calls melatonin 'a hormone'. Page 273: 'Melatonin acts through plasma membrane and nuclear receptors and by interaction with intracellular signalling proteins' (nuclear receptors not named). Book also calls melatonin a direct antioxidant and 'inductor of the antioxidant enzymes' (pages 272-273), with no named target, so not recorded.

records.quote: This finding lead to the design of specific agonists ramelteon (Rozerem®, Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Japan) and agomelatine (Valdoxan®, Servier and Novartis).
records.notes: The sentence does not repeat the receptor name; 'This finding' refers to the preceding sentences on MT1 and MT2 receptors. Book: 'approved by the FDA (July 2005) for the treatment of insomnia'.

records.mechanism_book_wording: specific agonists; binds to melatonin receptors
records.quote: This finding lead to the design of specific agonists ramelteon (Rozerem®, Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Japan) and agomelatine (Valdoxan®, Servier and Novartis).
records.notes: Same page, later sentence: 'Agomelatine binds to melatonin receptors'. Book gives a trade name (Valdoxan) but does not state approval status.

records.quote: Agomelatine binds to melatonin receptors but is also an antagonist of serotonin 5-HT2C receptors used to decrease anxiety and promote sleep

records.mechanism_book_wording: binds to nuclear receptors (VDRs) to modulate the transcription of genes
records.quote: The active form of vitamin D3 (1,25(OH)2-cholecalciferol or calcitriol) binds to nuclear receptors (VDRs) to modulate the transcription of genes
records.notes: The book says 'binds'; 'Agonist' is my inference, not a word on the page. drug_kind is my classification (book: 'the active form of vitamin D3'). In the print the 3 of D3 and the 2 of (OH)2 are subscripts. The sentence runs on to page 275, which also mentions 'fast, non genomic effects mediated by plasma membrane VDRs'.

records.role_detail: selective mTORC1 inhibition; requires formation of the rapamycin/FKBP12 complex, which interferes with the raptor-mTOR interaction
records.mechanism_book_wording: inhibits TOR; selectively and effectively inhibits mTORC1; inhibitor of mTORC1
records.quote: it mediates the effects of rapamycin, an antifungal and immunosuppressant agent that inhibits TOR.
records.notes: Book describes TOR as 'a serine/threonine protein kinase', hence enzyme. Book does not use the word 'approved'; it calls rapamycin 'an antifungal and immunosuppressant agent' and 'a macrolide antibiotic', so drug_kind is my reading. Page 282: 'The inhibitory action of rapamycin on TOR signaling requires the formation of the rapamycin/FKBP12 complex' (FKBP12 is named as a binding partner, no direction given, so no separate record). 'Rapamycin analogs (rapalogs)' are named on page 282 without a stated target.

records.quote: The firts CRM used was 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2DG), a compound that inhibits glycolisis.
records.notes: The book names a pathway, not a molecular target; a later reader may wish to drop this record. Typos 'firts' and 'glycolisis' are in the original. drug_kind is my reading (book: 'a compound', a caloric restriction mimetic tested in rodents).

records.mechanism_book_wording: activation of AMPK by the drug
records.quote: can also be due to the well recognized activation of AMPK by the drug
records.notes: Book calls metformin 'The biguanide antidiabetic drug' (page 281); 'approved' is my reading of that.

records.role_detail: indirect: via modulation of Rag signaling, or via AMPK activation
records.mechanism_book_wording: may inhibit mTORC1 via modulation of Rag signaling
records.quote: suggesting that this drug may inhibit mTORC1 via modulation of Rag signaling
records.notes: Hedged in the book ('suggesting', 'may'). Enzyme class follows the book's description of mTOR as a serine/threonine kinase (page 278); mTORC1 is a protein complex.

records.role_detail: suppression of activity in cells; book treats it as a downstream effect
records.quote: and to suppress S6K1 activity in cultured proliferating epithelial cells
records.notes: Not a direct-target statement: page 282 calls S6K1 the 'effector' of mTOR and attributes the effect to AMPK activation and mTORC1 inhibition. A later reader may wish to drop this record. Enzyme class from the book's 'kinase substrates (S6K and 4E-BP)' on page 279.

records.quote: are potent small-molecule activators of SIRT1 that are structurally unrelated to natural polyphenols
records.notes: Class record; no compound is named. Book: 'newly synthesized compounds' from Sirtris Pharmaceuticals, some 'in phase II clinical trials for type 2 diabetes' (page 283).

chapter_notes: Review chapter on anti-ageing interventions; body text is PDF pages 269-283, one figure (Fig. 1, page 280), no tables, reference list from page 283. No potency values are given; the only numbers are a 2DG dose and a melatonin formulation duration. Not recorded because no molecular target or direction is stated: antioxidants named only as such (vitamins E, A, C, deprenyl, NDGA, PBN, thioproline, flavonoids, catechins), growth hormone, buformin, phenformin, rapalogs, and 'caloric restriction mimetics' as a class; endogenous pathway statements between proteins (for example Akt on TSC2, AMPK on TORC1, amino acids on mTORC1) were also left out. Three records carry inferred or weak roles and say so in notes (melatonin and calcitriol 'Agonist'; 2DG pathway target; metformin on S6K1).
